derivedFrom: docs/measured-exhibit-palette.md — the eight approved exhibits, sampled 2026-09-29
rule: These tokens are measured from the artwork, not chosen. The 3D renderer consumes them and the Meshy style contract references them, so the room and its generator share one palette. Changing a token means the exhibits moved; re-measure before editing.

rim.role: pale bone rim on hero silhouettes

stylization.variantStatus: CHOSEN — operator ruling 2026-09-30. graphic-novel and woodcut are retained as reference points, not candidates.
stylization.openGap: Ink-line share measures 9.5% against an exhibit floor of 12.5%. This is NOT closed by widening the pen: a room of bare planes has nothing to draw. It closes in Phase 2, when the architecture gains timber framing, arches, shingle courses, and stone joints to ink.

contract.note: Bands a captured room must land inside to be congruent with the exhibit set. Derived from measurement (see docs/measured-exhibit-palette.md and scripts/recalibrate-gates.py), not chosen.
contract.derivation: Exhibit means, measured 2026-09-30: palette share 77.3% (range 65.1-86.2), ink share 8.3% (range 3.9-14.2), luminance 74-111, saturation 60-130.
contract.derivedInkLine: Exhibit ink-line share, measured with the same method: mean 20.6%, range 12.5-24.5%. The painted rooms measure 20.3-23.4%, i.e. inside the artwork's own range.
corrections: paletteShare was first set to 92%, which is unreachable: the exhibits themselves average 77.3% because a painting contains endless intermediate tones. The gate is now the artwork's own mean.

edge_density was first a gate at 24-46. It is not comparable between a painting and a rendered room: a painting is textured in every square inch, a room has large flat surfaces, so the mean tracks geometry rather than style. It is now informational only, and inkShare is the real ink gate.

character.note: Gates a generated Muse figure must pass before entering a room. See public/art/luma-canon.json.
